title: The Merciful taught
hookLine: the Merciful taught the Qur'an, created the human, taught him speech (55:1–4)
last: IS THERE ANY WHO WILL REMEMBER?

lines: A FIRST WORD STOPS THE KITCHEN.
cards: A toddler points at a dog and says a first word. Everyone in the kitchen stops. Someone grabs a phone to film it.
Nobody claps when a child first breathes on their own, or first digests a meal, but a first word gets a whole room cheering. Surah fifty-five opens with no oath and no mysterious letters.
It opens with one word, a name of God: Ar-Rahman, the Merciful. And the first things it says the Merciful did are about teaching, and about speech.

teach.h: AR-RAHMAN: ONE WORD, A WHOLE VERSE.
teach.b: Pickthall's first four verses: "The Beneficent / Hath made known the Qur'an. / He hath created man. / He hath taught him utterance." In Arabic, four short beats: Ar-Rahman. 'Allamal-Qur'an.
Notice the order: teaching the Qur'an comes before creating the human. Commentators have turned that over. Some read it as rank: guidance is named first as the greatest of the gifts that follow.
Others note the surah is a list of mercies, and the Qur'an is named before the one who receives it. Then what the human was taught: al-bayan, from the root b-y-n, to be clear, to stand apart.
Bayan is more than making sounds.

It's speech that makes something plain, that lets what's inside one person become clear to another. Commentators give it wide range: speech itself, the ability to explain, the power to tell good from bad and say why.
And all of it sits under the name Ar-Rahman. The surah frames speech as mercy. If it's a mercy, how it's used matters.

teach.h: SAY WHAT IS GOOD, OR STAY SILENT.
teach.b: A hadith in Bukhari puts it in one line: the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said that whoever believes in God and the Last Day should say what is good, or stay silent.
The same gift that names a dog in a kitchen can also wound, flatter or lie. The surah treats it as something given; the hadith, as something you answer for.

how: Many Muslims learn the opening verses of Surah Ar-Rahman by heart; the hadith on saying what is good or staying silent is often taught as a rule for everyday speech.

o: clear speech that makes what's inside plain
the beautiful sound of Qur'an recitation
the sermon given before Friday prayer

games.q: the opening of Ar-Rahman — tap the pairs.

s: Surah Ar-Rahman opens with an oath
it opens with a single name of God: Ar-Rahman.
in the opening verses, teaching the Qur'an is named before creating the human
commentators have long reflected on that order.
it's clear speech, the power to make something plain.

games.q: you're reading the first four verses of Ar-Rahman. which gift is named before the creation of the human?
games.why: the Merciful taught the Qur'an, then created the human, then taught him speech. some commentators read the order as a sign of rank.

practice: Bring to mind one person you'll talk to today, and something true and good about them you've never said out loud. Shape it into one plain sentence, the kind of bayan that makes something clear, and say it under your breath.

wordCard.voice: Bayan: clear speech, what the Merciful taught the human after teaching him the Qur'an and creating him, in the opening of Surah Ar-Rahman. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: He taught him clear speech. bayan comes from b-y-n, to be clear.

carryVoice: Your line: taught to speak. Speech is a gift, and a thing you answer for. Day six hundred three.
